newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields end mixed, crown stronger.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields end mixed, crown stronger.

text.p: Swedish long bond yields came off morning lows fairly quickly on Wednesday to close higher pushed by the weaker foreign markets.
"The sentiment is still very sour and nervous," said Knut Hallberg, economist at Swedbank Markets.
Market players were worried about Prime Minister Goran Persson comments about returning to traditional Social Democratic policies, which usually mean more spending.
Investment bank PaineWebber recommended a cautious approach when investing in the longer end of the curve.
Internationally EMU and whether the Fed will rise the rates at the next FOMC meeting continued to spread uncertainity and this spilt over to the Swedish market.
The U.S. February CPI-figure, that came in higher than exepcted, had an impact, pushing yields further up in Sweden.
Ten year bond yields rose one basis point to 7.48 percent, after opening some ten basis points lower.
The six-month T-bill rates, however, slid two basis points.
The crown received some support from commercial flows and picked up to 4.5600 against the mark from 4.6000 late Tuesday.
